hook: A rate of flow tells you how fast water enters a tank, minute by minute. To know how much water arrived, you need a function whose rate of change is that flow. Finding such a function, an antiderivative, turns every derivative rule around.

prereq.why: The power rule: bring the power down and lower it by one.
The Fundamental Theorem: an accumulation function has derivative $f$.

chain.cause: Adding a constant does not change a derivative
chain.effect: every $F(x) + C$ is an antiderivative too

chain.cause: The family of all of them is written $\int f(x)\,dx = F(x) + C$
chain.effect: an indefinite integral always carries $+ C$

ideas: Read each derivative rule backward to get an antiderivative rule.
Check an antiderivative by differentiating it.

misconception.right: That rule fails for $n = -1$, where the antiderivative is $\ln|x| + C$.

summary: An antiderivative undoes a derivative. The indefinite integral $\int f(x)\,dx = F(x) + C$ is the whole family of antiderivatives, and each derivative rule read backward is an antiderivative rule.
